notes: Page 2 shows steps 1-3. Step 1: red 2x2 plate (b1). Step 2: two dark bluish gray towball plates (b2, b3) on b1, with a light bluish gray socket plate (b4, b5) snapped onto each towball at the sides. Step 3: red 1x2 brick with 2 side studs (b6) placed on top.
The picture is small, so I inferred the step 2 piece identities (14417 + 14704) and placement. The socket plates are attached only by ball/socket, so they rest on nothing.
I assumed b6 lies crosswise and bridges b2 and b3, so it rests on both. Its stud ports on the first row of b2 and the second row of b3 are a guess.

Page 3 shows steps 4 and 5. Each builds a mirrored arm sub-assembly: a red hinge plate 1x4 swivel, a red 1x1 clip plate on one end stud, and a red curved 2x1 brick on top. Step 4 builds the left arm (b7-b9). Step 5 builds the mirror-image right arm (b10-b12).

I couldn't tell how each arm attaches to the body. I assumed the step 4 hinge plate clutches onto the side studs of b6, and the step 5 hinge plate onto b6's top studs. Both are guesses and may need correcting from later pages.
The catalogue lists only stud.1.1 and stud.1.2 for the hinge plate, so the clip plate goes on stud.1.1 and the curved brick on stud.1.2. The real curved brick probably covers two studs.
Page 4 shows steps 6-7 with the model turned to a new angle. Step 6 places one red 1x2 plate (b13) on two studs on top of the body. I assumed those are the top studs of b6.
Step 7 has no callout and no arrow, and I could not see a new piece in it. It looks like the same model turned so a red face with 4 studs shows. I added nothing for step 7.
The step 5 guess that b10 sits on b6's top studs conflicts with b13 using those same studs. The step 4 and 5 attachments may need revising once later pages clarify how the arms attach.
Page 5 shows steps 8-9. Step 8 adds a dark red 2x4 wedge plate (b14) on top of the model. Step 9 shows the same model with no new piece, so I added nothing for it.
I assumed the wedge clutches the two studs of the red 1x2 plate b13 on top. It may also touch other pieces. The picture is too small to tell.
Page 6 shows steps 10-11. Step 10 is the same model turned to a new angle, with no new piece. Step 11 adds one dark red cheese slope (b15) on a top stud.

The picture is too small to tell which piece carries the target stud. I assumed b13, the red 1x2 plate. It could instead be a stud on b6 or the wedge b14. I used b13 stud.1.1 even though b14 also uses it in my earlier guess, so this may need revising.

Page 7 shows steps 12-13. Step 12 has no callout, but the model now has a dark red slope on the right side as well. I took that to be a second cheese slope (b16) mirroring b15, placed on b13's second stud. This is a guess.

Step 13 adds the black handlebars (b18) onto a red 1x1 tile with clip (b17). Its picture looks like the red 1x1 tile with clip (12825), the only unused red clip piece, so I used that type. I assumed it sits on b15's stud, though the picture suggests the top centre of the model.
The handlebars-to-clip join is recorded as pin.1 to clip.1, revolute, since the handlebar bar can turn in the clip.
Page 8 shows step 14, which adds two googly eyes (white ball joints with the black eye print, b19 and b20), one on each side of the handlebars.

I assumed each eye sits on top of one of the dark red cheese slopes (b15 left, b16 right) through its axle-hole. The picture doesn't show the join. This conflicts with my earlier guess that the clip tile b17 sits on b15, so the real stud positions need checking against later pages.

Page 9 shows steps 15-16. Step 15's callout is a red 1x2 30° slope (b22). The white tri-tooth plate (b21) first appears on the model in this step with no callout of its own, so I added it here as the teeth.
I assumed b21 clutches b6's side studs and the red slope sits on top of b21. The side studs are already used by b7 in my step 4 guess, so that earlier guess likely needs revising.

Step 16 has no callout, but the model visibly gains a dark red band across the jaw and a dark red trapezoid below. These are probably the unused dark red curved 4x1 brick (93273) and the second dark red wedge plate (51739). I couldn't tell how they attach, so I added nothing for step 16. Those parts may show up on a later page.

Page 10 starts a separate sub-model, a leg with a ball at the end. The top-left picture shows the finished sub-model, and there is no 2x box, so I built it once. It has not been attached to the body yet.

Step 1: a dark bluish gray plate with a ball (b23) gets a red 65° slope on its two studs. Step 2: a dark red cheese slope goes on top of the 65° slope. Step 3: a red inverted slope (b26) goes under the plate.
Both 14417 pieces are already used as b2 and b3, so I took the grey plate with the ball to be a 14419 (dark bluish gray, with towball). If page 2's plates were actually 14419, this should be 14417.
The catalogue lists only anti ports for the inverted slope (3665), but the picture shows studs on it. I left its port null on the plate-to-slope join.

Page 11 shows leg step 4 and main model step 17. Leg step 4: a second dark bluish gray ball plate (b27) gets a red 1x2 plate (b28) on its studs, and the pair is attached to the front of the leg as the foot. The leg is 14419 (b23) and this plate is 14417, matching the inventory counts.
I assumed b27's anti-studs clutch b26's studs, since the picture shows b27 at the front-bottom of the leg. The catalogue has no stud ports for 3665, so the port is null.

Step 17 attaches the finished leg to the body at the lower side. The arrow points at the leg, not at a specific socket. I recorded b27's ball going into socket b5 on the body, but b5 is already on b3's towball in my page 2 guess, so this is probably wrong and needs checking.
Page 12 builds the second leg sub-model, a mirror of the page 10 leg. It uses the same steps: ball plate, red 65° slope, dark red cheese slope on top, red inverted slope underneath.
I took the plate to be the second 14419, since 14417 appears to be used by b2, b3 and b27. This leg is not attached to the body yet.
Page 13 shows leg 2 step 4 and main model step 18. Leg 2 step 4 repeats page 11's step 4: a ball plate (b33) with a red 1x2 plate (b34) on top, attached to the front of the leg as the foot.

Step 18 attaches the second leg to the body's other side. I mirrored step 17 and recorded b33's ball into socket b4. Like b5 in step 17, b4 is already used by b2's towball in my page 2 guess, so this is probably wrong.

The inventory has only four dark bluish gray ball plates (2 x 14417 and 2 x 14419), yet I've now used b2, b3, b27 and b33 as 14417 plus b23 and b29 as 14419. So b2 and b3 on page 2 are probably misidentified.
Page 14 shows step 19, which only has the rotate-model icon, so it has no new pieces and I added nothing.

The rotated back view already shows two trans-red/yellow flame pieces (85959). They have no callout on this page, so they are probably added on a later page, or they are the two clip tile pieces from earlier steps. I did not record them here. If the next page adds the flames, they will clip onto the back of the model.
Page 15 only shows the rotate-model icon and the model turned to another angle. It has no callout or new piece, so nothing is added.
The flames are still visible on the model but no flame piece has been called out yet. I haven't recorded them. A later page should show how they attach.
Page 17 is an advertising page (Infernites Max combination, lego.com/mixels). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 16 was skipped, so I have not seen it. The flame pieces (85959pat0003 x2) have still not been attached in any page I've seen, so they might be on page 16 or a later page.
Page 18 is an advertising page listing the Mixels collection (sets 41500-41526). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 19 is a game advertisement with an in-game code. It has no building steps, so nothing is added.
Page 20 is the back cover (product feedback survey, legal text). It has no building steps, so nothing is added.

The booklet is finished, but the graph has gaps. The two flame pieces (lego-85959pat0003) and the dark red curved 4x1 brick (lego-93273) were never placed. The second dark red wedge plate (lego-51739) was also never placed. The jaw band and bottom wedge seen at step 16 and the flames seen at steps 19-20 therefore have no pieces or edges. Pages 14-16 and the pages in between may need another look.

Several attachments in my earlier turns were guesses and conflict: the arm joins on b6, the sockets b4 and b5 reused for the legs, and the eye and clip-tile studs on b15 and b16. These should be revised if you can check the original booklet.

The parts check showed the 14417 count was wrong. It said 14417 was used 2 times too many, which means b2 and b3 from page 2 were misread. The inventory has only 2 x 14417, and b27 and b33 (the feet) use both. I re-declared b2 as the black bracket 44728 (the black 2x2 face with studs seen on pages 4-9) and b3 as the red inverted bracket 99207 (the red 4-stud face first visible at step 7). That fixes the type counts for 14417, 44728 and 99207.

This turn re-declares b2 and b3 with new types. Their old page 2 edges (b2 and b3 anti ports onto b1's studs, b4/b5 socket to b2/b3 ball, b6 on b2/b3) are still in the graph. Those edges are stale. Replace them and drop the b4/b5 ball joins (b2/b3 have no ball). The sockets b4/b5 are likely clipped onto other pieces.

Pieces added to match the parts list: 3020 x1, 3069b x2, 3710 x1, 3794b x3, 51739 (second), 85959pat0003 x2, 93273 x1. The booklet pages for these (probably page 16 and the unseen steps) were not shown to me. The placements are guesses, mainly from the finished-model pictures.

Guesses: the 93273 jaw band sits on the wedge b14's free studs; the second 51739 wedge goes on b2's face studs as the trapezoid below the jaw; the flames clip onto the arm clips b8 and b11; the 3069b tiles cap the foot plates b28 and b34. The 3020, 3710 and three 3794b are put together as an underside or back assembly under b1. Their true positions are unknown.
Not a real problem: the 14419 and 14704 counts, and all other pieces, match the inventory.

My last turn tried to re-declare b2 and b3 with new types, which was not accepted because given pieces stay as they are. This turn adds the black bracket (b46, lego-44728) and the red inverted bracket (b47, lego-99207) as new pieces. That covers the two missing parts.

The excess of lego-14417 x2 is a real problem and I cannot remove it with additions only. b2 and b3 (page 2) were misidentified. They should be deleted and are superseded by b46 and b47. The inventory has only 2 x 14417, and b27 and b33 (the feet) use both. When b2 and b3 are dropped, the b4 and b5 socket joins to b2 and b3 and the b6 joins to them should go too.

Placement of b46 and b47 is a guess: b46 sits on b1's first-row studs, b47 sits on b46's top studs (the red 4-stud face seen at step 7), and the second wedge b42 is moved onto b46's face studs, replacing the b42-to-b2 edges from last turn. The old b42-to-b2 edges, b6 joins and b13 joins refer to the removed b2 and b3 and should be repointed to b46 and b47.
